1. First, calculate the total area of the five-by-five square.
   \[
   \text{Total area} = 5 \times 5 = 25 \text{ square units}
   \]

2. Next, determine the area of the shaded regions. Observing the diagram, we see that there are 10 shaded squares. Each shaded square is 1 unit by 1 unit.
   \[
   \text{Area of one shaded square} = 1 \times 1 = 1 \text{ square unit}
   \]
   \[
   \text{Total shaded area} = 10 \times 1 = 10 \text{ square units}
   \]

3. Now, calculate the percentage of the square that is shaded.
   \[
   \text{Percentage shaded} = \left( \frac{\text{Total shaded area}}{\text{Total area}} \right) \times 100 = \left( \frac{10}{25} \right) \times 100 = 40\%
   \]

Therefore, \(\boxed{40\%}\).
